value: strongly attracted to water scented by zebra mussel, but not to water scented by fish
units: categorical (two-choice scent test; paired t-test P values)

source.authors: Matteo Rolla, Sofia Consuegra, Eleanor Carrington, David J. Hall, Carlos Garcia de Leaniz
source.title: Experimental evidence of chemical attraction in the mutualistic zebra mussel-killer shrimp system

method: behavioural: two-choice fluviarium, scented water (zebra mussel, Nile tilapia or blank) versus blank, paired t-tests
conditions: Wild-collected killer shrimp held in laboratory tanks at Swansea University; sympatric animals from Cardiff Bay and allopatric animals from Upper Mother Ditch (no zebra mussels). Scents: zebra mussels or tilapia held 24 h in dechlorinated water at 50 g/L biomass, delivered at 200 ml/min (tool summary). Experiment 3 tested blank versus blank, blank versus tilapia scent and blank versus zebra mussel scent in each population; each shrimp acclimatised for 5 min and time in each arm was then recorded for 15 min; the fluviarium was drained and cleaned with 90% ethanol between trials; the page does not describe side randomisation for this experiment or say whether shrimp were tested only once. Blank versus blank showed no side bias (sympatric t9 = 1.343, P = 0.212; allopatric t19 = -1.280, P = 0.216). Shrimp were held in recirculating tanks at 15-16.5 C and fed frozen bloodworms three times a week; holding time and pre-test fasting are not reported. Results sentences read in abutting pieces: with tilapia scent 'no preference was observed over blank water, either in sympatry (t19 = 0.819, P = 0.423; Fig. 5C) or allopatry (t19 = - 0.687, P = 0.500; Fig. 5D)'; for zebra mussel scent, attraction in the sympatric (t27 = - 2.176, P = 0.038) and allopatric population (t19 = - 2.614, P = 0.017), no population difference (F1,118 = 1.036, P = 0.311; verbatim, audit 346). Sample sizes do not reconcile in the page: Methods give n = 60 per population, the Figure 5 caption n = 40 per scent treatment, and the t-test degrees of freedom imply 10, 20 and 28 sympatric and 20, 20 and 20 allopatric shrimp for the blank, tilapia and zebra mussel tests. Scent strength is a prepared biomass dose; no concentration of chemical cues measured. The same paper's other experiments (settlement on mussel mats, not different from artificial grass) are not part of this value.
quote: Killer shrimp were strongly attracted to water scented by zebra mussel, but not to water scented by fish.

value: males visited capture webs spun by old females significantly more than webs of younger females, in trials with webs alone
units: categorical (male visits to webs; Fisher exact test)

source.title: Old maids have more appeal: effects of age and pheromone source on mate attraction in an orb-web spider

method: behavioural: field test of male attraction to a neutral web carrying a female's body or to the female's own web alone, three female age classes, two-hour trials, Fisher exact test
conditions: Females were collected as juveniles and sub-adults from a natural meadow near Nebenstedt, reared in the laboratory and tested in the field (Buxtehude, Lower Saxony, 12-26 July 2012; tool summary), so the females were wild-origin and the visiting males were free-living (Methods do not say where the males came from; males were released a few metres away after each test). Age classes young (1-2 days after maturation), middle-aged (3-7), old (8 or more); each female in one class. Web trials: 14 young, 14 middle-aged, 13 old (tool summary). Females were virgins; webs of sub-adult females served as neutral webs on the authors' statement that they contain no pheromone; each web was observed for two hours in the field, with web categories at least eight metres apart or tested at different times, and males that tried to reach a female or web for at least 5 min were counted. Results read in abutting pieces: webs of old females (6 of 13 webs) 'attracted males significantly more often than webs of young females and webs of middle-aged females (for both pairwise comparisons we used the same statistic: N = 27, p = 0.0329, Fig. 1)'. Only one web of young females and one of middle-aged females was visited, so each class was compared only with old females (Fisher exact tests). Nulls and other results from the same Results: a paired comparison of male visitors attracted by a given female in a neutral web and by her own web was not significant (Wilcoxon T = 58.5, N = 14, p = 0.3724). Only 23 of 77 females or webs were visited by males during the 2 h observation (verbatim, audit 346). In trials with females placed in neutral webs, only young and old females differed (N = 24, p = 0.0361), and age was not significantly correlated with the number of male visitors (rs = 0.49, N = 13, p = 0.0909; tool summary). The design does not separate airborne from contact cues on the silk. The compound responsible was not identified; attraction to a web is attributed to pheromone by the authors.
quote: Capture webs alone spun by old females were significantly more efficient in attracting males than webs of younger females.
note: Whole abstract sentence of 19 words, returned intact in two passes. value: bait taken in 33% of trials with the Scuba7 electric deterrent switched on versus 100% of trials with it off
units: percent of trials with bait taken

source.authors: Madeline Thiele, Johann Mourier, Yannis Papastamatiou, Laurent Ballesta, Eric Chateauminois, Charlie Huveneers
source.title: Response of blacktip reef sharks Carcharhinus melanopterus to shark bite mitigation products

method: behavioural: baited field trials with a commercial electric deterrent (Ocean Guardian Scuba7) randomly switched on or off in blocks of two, video scored single-blind, GLMM
conditions: Free-ranging blacktip reef sharks at Fakarava Atoll, French Polynesia, where locals feed the sharks daily, so the sharks were habituated to provisioning. Seven consecutive days in June 2017, 12 trials per day, status block-randomised before each set of two trials (Methods piece), 84 trials (42 on, 42 off) with 966 approaches (tool summary; approaches per trial 3.62 +/- 0.53 vs 19.38 +/- 2.29, more with the device on); trials up to three minutes. Results pieces: 'When the Scuba7 was inactive, sharks took the bait during all trials' and 'In contrast, sharks took the bait on 33% of the trials'; device status significantly affected all response variables (Table 1 not read). Also from tool summary: time to take bait 38.9 +/- 3.35 s (off) vs 165 +/- 20.40 s (on); approach distance 38.88 +/- 3.20 cm vs 80.98 +/- 1.72 cm. Electric field was modelled, not measured: electrodes treated as point charges 1.7 m apart; about 1 V/m about 1.1 m horizontally from the electrodes in mid-water, 7-16 V/m 80 cm from the electrodes, up to 80 V/m as sharks swam over the electrodes and nearly 115 V/m at the electrodes over non-conductive seabed. The Scuba7's voltage, pulse rate and frequency are not reported. Individual sharks could not be identified (no distinguishable markings or scars), so the number of sharks tested and repeat exposure of the same sharks are unknown; up to 24 sharks were sighted within 30 m of the bait, and Day was a random effect in the binomial GLMM. The authors note that regular feeding by locals may have reduced competition; no test of habituation to the device over the seven days is reported. The authors state the device targets the ampullae of Lorenzini, which the study does not test. A second experiment (Kevlar-neoprene bite pouches) is not part of this value. The response is to a prepared deterrent next to bait, not a detection threshold.
quote: The Scuba7 reduced the proportion of baits being taken by 67%, (from 100% during control trials to 33%).

value: free-living rats did not avoid boxes with predator odour and showed no increase in latency of food carrying or other fear-related behaviour (null)
units: categorical (compartment choice and food-carrying latency; Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis P values)

source.authors: Rafał Stryjek, Berenika Mioduszewska, Ewelina Spaltabaka-Gędek, Grzegorz R. Juszczak
source.title: Wild Norway Rats Do Not Avoid Predator Scents When Collecting Food in a Familiar Habitat: A Field Study

method: behavioural: field choice between two food compartments, one with cardboard soaked in predator scent and one with water, Mann-Whitney, Kruskal-Wallis and Friedman tests
conditions: Free-living colony on a farm on the outskirts of Warsaw, Poland (about 40-50 rats; animals unmarked, so exact sample size and composition are unknown and the same individuals were probably sampled repeatedly). Pen in a barn (200 x 100 x 100 cm) entered from burrows; central box with two compartments each with a food bowl; scented bowls alternated left and right; 7 days of habituation with unscented pellets, then each of nine odours for 3-5 consecutive days with 2 unscented days between odours, 20 January to 18 March (tool summary). Odours: urine of cat, dog and fox (sympatric) and of mountain lion, African lion, Sumatran tiger and coyote (allopatric; Methods sentence read in two pieces), plus lion faeces and TMT (tool summary). Results read in pieces: no difference between compartments in pellet pace (Mann-Whitney U = 605, P = 0.93) and no difference among the nine odours (Kruskal-Wallis chi2(8, N = 35) = 12.97, P = 0.113). Single-dose, single-site, familiar territory next to burrows; the authors limit the conclusion to foraging near shelter in familiar territory. Odour concentration not measured; urine (1 ml) and lion faeces (1 ml of water solution) were smeared on the cardboard, and TMT was given from three 10 ul pipette tips fixed to the bowl. Also null: instances where pellets were approached but none picked did not differ between compartments (U = 521, P = 0.113); latency to the first pellet across stages, Friedman chi2(7, N = 4) = 12.303, P = 0.09. The paper does not define N in the Kruskal-Wallis test. The authors state the study used a single wild colony, which limits general conclusions, and list parasite infection, design, habituation and individual differences as alternative explanations (tool summary). A null of avoidance does not show that the odours went undetected.
quote: The rats did not avoid boxes with predator odor and did not display an increased latency of food-carrying behavior or any other fear-related behavior, such as freezing or increased grooming.

value: beetles were attracted in field assays to a blend of DMTS, 3-octanone and benzaldehyde
units: categorical (pitfall-trap catch with synthetic odour blends; Kruskal-Wallis with Nemenyi post hoc)

source.authors: Sandra Weithmann, Christian von Hoermann, Thomas Schmitt, Sandra Steiger, Manfred Ayasse
source.title: The Attraction of the Dung Beetle Anoplotrupes stercorosus (Coleoptera: Geotrupidae) to Volatiles from Vertebrate Cadavers

method: field behavioural: pitfall traps baited with synthetic blends derived from cadaver headspace, compared with a negative control and piglet tissue, Kruskal-Wallis test
conditions: Free-living beetles trapped in August 2018 on five Biodiversity Exploratories forest plots in the Schwäbische Alb, Germany (the separate GC-EAD beetles were caught near Darmstadt): five 100 x 100 m plots with five pitfall traps each, one treatment per trap (full six-compound mix, blend 2 = benzaldehyde + DMTS + 3-octanone, blend 3 = 6-methyl-5-hepten-2-ol + nonanal + dodecane, piglet tissue positive control, empty-tube negative control), 48 h per baiting event, five events, treatments rotated clockwise after each event so no trap kept a treatment (paper does not describe random assignment); n = 25 trap-events per treatment (tool summary). Trap fluid was a scent-free detergent/water solution (Methods piece). Results pieces: totals were 74 (complete mixture), 94 (blend 2), 14 (blend 3), 7 (negative control), 34 (positive control); 'The treatments had a significant effect on the total beetle abundance per trap (Kruskal-Wallis test: chi2 = 31.077, df = 4, p < 0.001'. Per tool summary: blend 2 differed from the negative control (p < 0.001) and from blend 3 (p = 0.002), the complete mixture differed from the negative control (p = 0.005), and blend 2 and the complete mixture did not differ. Blend 3 caught 14 against 7 in the negative control (the paper calls its low attractiveness unclear); no compound was tested alone, and the main text gives no per-compound amounts (about 250 ul per blend, pipetting scheme in Table S1, not read; tool summary), so each blend was tested at one dose. Both synthetic blends caught more beetles than the piglet-tissue positive control (94 and 74 against 34); no post hoc p value is printed for blend 3 against the controls. Treatment counts sum to 223 against 220 stated in the text (tool summary).
quote: In field assays, these beetles were attracted to a blend of DMTS, 3-octanone, and benzaldehyde.

value: antennae responded to 24 volatiles in odour bouquets from post-bloating decay (GC-EAD)

source.authors: Sandra Weithmann, Christian von Hoermann, Thomas Schmitt, Sandra Steiger, Manfred Ayasse
source.title: The Attraction of the Dung Beetle Anoplotrupes stercorosus (Coleoptera: Geotrupidae) to Volatiles from Vertebrate Cadavers

method: gas chromatography with electroantennographic detection (GC-EAD) of headspace from piglet cadavers at post-bloating decay; peaks scored active only with at least 5 reproducible responses (tool summary)
conditions: Eight living wild-caught beetles from near Darmstadt, Germany, one antenna per beetle (Methods pieces: 'We used antennae of eight living dung beetles (Anoplotrupes stercorosus) that were caught near Darmstadt, Germany,' and 'One antenna per beetle was used for GC-EAD recordings.'). Cadavers were frozen stillborn domestic piglets exposed for one week in wire cages, headspace sampled on day 6 (tool summary). Compounds identified by GC-MS against NIST11 library and retention indices. The count is of responsive compounds in a pooled bouquet, not a sensitivity threshold; which of the 24 drive behaviour is tested separately in the field record.
